” Namely, we want a (signed) discrete measure μ that is supported at (finitely or countably many) real numbers aₙ so that
  ∫ xᵐ dμ(x) = m   for every m = 1, 2, 3, … .

Writing μ as
  μ = Σₙ δ₍ₐₙ₎      (where δ₍ₐₙ₎ is a Dirac mass at aₙ),
this is exactly the condition that the sequence (aₙ) has the desired property.

sentence: A classical theorem about moment problems (sometimes in connection with the Hahn–Banach theorem or the Riesz representation theorem) shows that if you specify “moments” (here m for the mth moment) that grow sufficiently slowly the representing measure exists.
